header.title: Machabaeorum ii: AI translation (Claude)
header.author: Old Testament
header.source: Translated by Claude (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic) from the library's tlg0527.tlg024.1st1K-grc1, from Open Greek and Latin's First1KGreek (CC BY-SA 4.0), one English line for each line of the original. Only some passages are translated so far: those that the Atlas of Ancient Myth, Magic in the Ancient Texts and the demons-and-angels study cite.
header.statement: An AI-generated translation. No specialist has reviewed it.

notes.urn:cts:greekLit:tlg0527.tlg024.1st1K-gr: The text gives Nephthar for both names; after 'but' a different form is expected, so the second may be corrupt.
Ῥύθην is read as ῥύδην, 'with a rush'. τὴν γλῶσσαν, 'in speech' (literally 'in tongue'), is odd where their looks are being described, and may be corrupt.

nodes.text: And when this had been done and some time had passed, and the sun, which had been clouded over, shone out, a great blaze was kindled, so that all marvelled.
Those with Nehemiah called this Nephthar, which is interpreted Purification; but by most people it is called Nephthar.

For there appeared to them a horse with a fearsome rider, adorned with the most beautiful trappings, and charging furiously it lashed at Heliodorus with its front hooves; and the rider was seen to have full armour of gold.

Two other young men also appeared to him, outstanding in strength, most fair in speech, splendid in their dress; they stood on either side of him and flogged him without ceasing, laying many blows on him.

And under the tunics of each of the dead they found sacred objects of the idols of Jamnia, from which the law kept the Jews away; and it became clear to all that it was for this reason that these men had fallen.
